problems.title: Design Tic Tac Toe
problems.summary: Play on an N x N board with O(1) win detection using per-line counters instead of scanning, and a bot whose difficulty is a swappable strategy — random, or a minimax player that provably never loses.
concepts: O(1) win detection with incremental line counters
Undo on the board so minimax can explore without copying it
Separating who moves from how a bot decides
Depth-aware minimax scoring, and alpha-beta pruning
Injecting the input source so a human player is testable
extensions: Generalise to k-in-a-row on an N x N board
Add more than two players
Add undo and redo for human players
Add a medium-difficulty bot that makes deliberate mistakes
Persist and resume a game in progress

problems.title: Snake and Ladder
problems.summary: Build a turn-based Snake and Ladder game where the die can be swapped between fair and crooked without touching the game loop, and the board refuses layouts where one jump chains into another.
concepts: Dependency injection for randomness
Validating invariants at construction rather than at use
Returning values instead of printing, so the domain is testable
extensions: Rolling a six earns the player another turn
Place snakes and ladders randomly at setup while keeping the no-chain rule
Support rolling more than one die per turn
Undo the last move
Save and resume a game in progress

problems.title: Design Splitwise
problems.summary: Track shared expenses across four split types where every split sums exactly to the total, keep one net balance per person instead of a debt matrix, and settle the whole group in at most n-1 payments.
concepts: Integer money, and why floats break ledgers slowly
The largest remainder method for splits that do not divide evenly
Net balances instead of a who-owes-whom matrix
Greedy debt settlement, its n-1 bound, and why the true minimum is NP-hard
Freezing derived values so history cannot be rewritten
extensions: Support multiple currencies and decide which exchange rate applies
Add groups, and decide whether balances are per group or global
Allow editing and deleting past expenses
Rotate who absorbs the rounding remainder across expenses
Restrict settlement suggestions to within a group
Handle concurrent expense creation

problems.title: Design a Logging Framework
problems.summary: Route log records down a handler chain where every link applies its own threshold and format, so one chain can send everything to the console and only errors to a JSON file — and where the chain deliberately does not stop at the first handler that takes it.
concepts: Adapting a pattern rather than copying it: why a logging chain must not stop
Two thresholds serving different purposes: a cheap gate and per-sink filtering
Keeping format independent of destination to avoid a class per combination
When Singleton is genuinely correct, and what it costs in testability
Bound context for correlating records across a request
extensions: Make delivery asynchronous with a queue and a writer thread
Rotate log files by size or date
Rate-limit repeated identical messages with a decorating handler
Support hierarchical loggers that inherit handlers from their parent
Make handlers safe for concurrent writers
Redact secrets before records are written

problems.title: Design a Notification Service
problems.summary: Fan a message out to email, SMS, push and Slack according to each subscriber's per-channel priority threshold, with retry, rate limiting and deduplication written once as decorators that compose around any channel.
concepts: Cross-cutting policy as decorators rather than duplicated per channel
Why decorator stacking order changes behaviour
Distinguishing a deliberate suppression from a retryable failure
Per-channel delivery preferences, not per-user
Injecting transports and clocks so delivery policy is testable
extensions: Deliver asynchronously through a queue with a dead letter queue
Add templating and localisation for message bodies
Fall back to the next channel when the preferred one fails
Add scheduled and digest notifications
Add a circuit breaker so a dead provider is not hammered
Respect per-user quiet hours and time zones

problems.title: Design a Parking Lot
problems.summary: Assign spots to arriving vehicles by a pluggable allocation strategy, charge for the stay on exit by a separate pricing strategy, and drive the whole thing from a command console where adding an operation never edits an existing one.
concepts: Subclass versus constructor argument: when a difference is data, not behaviour
Deriving counts instead of maintaining a parallel counter
Injecting the clock so duration-based logic is testable
Open/closed dispatch through a command registry
extensions: Make the lot safe for concurrent gates
Support multiple floors
Handle vehicles that occupy more than one spot
Allow a spot to be reserved ahead of arrival
Add surge pricing at peak hours by decorating a pricing strategy
Persist the lot state across restarts

problems.title: Design a Rate Limiter
problems.summary: Implement token bucket, fixed window, sliding window log and sliding window counter behind one interface, and be able to say what each one gets wrong — starting with the boundary burst that lets a fixed window pass double its limit.
concepts: Memory versus accuracy trade-offs between limiting algorithms
The fixed-window boundary burst, and two ways to fix it
Lazy token refill so idle clients cost nothing to track
Passing time in as a parameter so time-based logic is testable
Bounding per-client state so the bucket map is not a leak
extensions: Distribute the limiter across servers using Redis
Support different limits per customer tier
Limit on several keys at once (user, IP and endpoint)
Decide whether to fail open or fail closed when the limiter is unavailable
Emit standard X-RateLimit and Retry-After headers

problems.title: Design a Text Editor with Undo
problems.summary: Build an editor whose every edit is a reversible command, where consecutive keystrokes coalesce into one undo step, replace-all undoes as a single action, and a new edit after an undo correctly discards the redo stack.
concepts: Command versus Memento for undo, and the memory trade between them
Why a new edit must clear the redo stack
Coalescing keystrokes so undo matches what a user considers one action
Composite commands undoing in reverse order
Capturing inverse data at execute time, not construction time
Bounding the undo stack so a long session is not a leak
extensions: Add a piece table or rope so large files do not copy the whole string
Support multiple cursors editing at once
Add collaborative editing with operational transforms or CRDTs
Add syntax highlighting as a decorator over the document
Persist the undo history across sessions
Add a non-linear undo tree rather than a single stack

problems.title: Design a Vending Machine
problems.summary: Model a vending machine as an explicit state machine where each state decides which actions it accepts, and where a machine that cannot make change leaves the item on the shelf and the buyer's money untouched.
concepts: Default-refuse base class so each state only writes what it supports
Ordering operations so a failure leaves no partial change behind
Escrow: refunding the coins inserted rather than making change
Integer money, and the limits of greedy change-making
extensions: Accept card payment alongside coins
Show an 'exact change only' indicator before money is inserted
Make the machine safe for concurrent buyers
Record a purchase history using Observer
Return the balance automatically after a period of inactivity

problems.title: Design an ATM
problems.summary: Model an ATM as a state machine where each state permits only what is safe from it, and build the note dispenser as a chain of denomination handlers that plans the full amount before a single note leaves the box.
concepts: States as a security boundary, not just a convenience
All-or-nothing dispensing: planning against a copy before committing
Ordering a debit and a dispense so a failure never costs the customer
Keeping the bank separate from the machine so it can be stubbed
Greedy note selection, and when it stops being correct
extensions: Add a transaction log that survives a power cut mid-dispense
Support multiple currencies in one machine
Add card types with different daily limits and fees
Handle a network outage to the bank with offline limits
Make the machine safe against concurrent sessions on a shared cash box
Add receipt printing and mini-statements

problems.title: Design an In-Memory File System
problems.summary: Model files and directories as one composite tree so no caller ever branches on which it is holding, then add search, disk usage and rendering as visitors that walk the tree without living on it.
concepts: Composite: a uniform interface over leaves and containers
Why two typed child lists force every traversal to be written twice
Deriving size recursively instead of caching and invalidating it
Visitor's trade: cheap new operations, expensive new node types
Lazy traversal with generators over materialising the whole tree
Resolving . and .. during the walk so .. cannot escape the root
extensions: Add symbolic links, and decide what they do to recursive size
Add permissions and ownership per node
Add copy-on-write snapshots of a subtree
Support file handles with seek, read and write offsets
Cache directory sizes correctly, invalidating up the ancestor chain
Make the tree safe for concurrent readers and writers

problems.title: Design an LRU Cache
problems.summary: Build a fixed-capacity cache with O(1) get and put, backed by a hand-written doubly linked list, whose eviction rule swaps between LRU, LFU and FIFO without the cache learning what any of them mean.
concepts: Hash map plus doubly linked list for O(1) reordering
Sentinel nodes to remove null checks from pointer surgery
O(1) LFU via frequency buckets and an incrementally tracked minimum
Overwrite is not insert: why treating it as one empties the cache
Injecting the clock so TTL tests do not sleep
extensions: Make the cache thread-safe, then shard it by key hash
Bound capacity by bytes rather than entry count
Add write-through to a backing store
Expire keys eagerly with a background sweep instead of on read
Support per-tenant caches under one global capacity limit

problems.title: Design Chess
problems.summary: Give each piece responsibility for how it moves, make every move an undoable command, and decide legality by playing a move and asking whether your own king is now attacked — verified against known perft counts to depth four.
concepts: Pseudo-legal versus legal moves, and why the split is necessary
Make/unmake as the mechanism that makes legality decidable
Capturing everything a move needs to reverse itself, at the time it is made
Why a pawn's attacks differ from its moves
Deriving game status from the position rather than caching it
Perft as a correctness check on move generation
extensions: Add threefold repetition as a draw condition
Import and export FEN and PGN
Add an engine with minimax and alpha-beta over this move generator
Switch to bitboards and measure the difference against perft
Support variants such as Chess960 where castling squares differ
Add a clock with increment and flag-fall

problems.title: Design an Elevator System
problems.summary: Run a bank of elevators where each car follows the LOOK algorithm — sweep one way serving every stop, reverse only when nothing is ahead — and the choice of which car answers a hall call is a strategy that can be tuned without any car noticing.
concepts: The LOOK/SCAN algorithm, and why nearest-first starves riders
Serving a stop only in the direction the rider wants to travel
Hall calls and car calls as genuinely different request types
Separating which car is chosen from how a car behaves once chosen
Tick-based simulation so scheduling is testable without threads
Wall-clock time versus total distance as competing objectives
extensions: Run each elevator on its own thread with a real controller
Add weight-based capacity so a full car skips hall calls
Add express elevators that serve only some floors
Add emergency and fire-service modes that override scheduling
Add destination dispatch, where riders enter their floor in the lobby
Handle a car that fails mid-journey and reassign its riders
